title: Opportunity Surface + Cost-Delta Prioritization: roadmap scorer for latency-sensitive inference features
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current RICE-based prioritization overweights raw reach and effort without directly modeling the token-level cost and latency impact of inference features. For Redwood, many product decisions (e.g., structured output, function calling, new streaming modes) trade off customer-perceived latency and per-token cost.

Goal: Produce a pragmatic hybrid prioritization rubric ("Opportunity Surface + Cost-Delta") that combines RICE-style signals with per-initiative delta in latency and token-dollar economics, so PMs can rank initiatives by expected customer value per incremental cost while accounting for SLO risk. The rubric should be lightweight for cycle planning, auditable for stakeholders, and compatible with existing OKR tracking.

Scope: Prototype scoring for the next 3-cycle roadmap (Q2 planning). Provide exemplar scored initiatives (3–5) and guidance for PMs to apply the model. Deliverables: scoring template (CSV/Google Sheet), evaluator checklist, and a short playbook section for roadmap review meetings.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible scoring spreadsheet that calculates final priority rank and shows component breakdown (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort, LatencyPenalty, CostDelta)
Three example initiatives scored end-to-end with annotated assumptions and links to supporting artifacts
Playbook doc for PMs with step-by-step scoring instructions and decision thresholds
Sign-off from two PMs and one engineering lead (ENG-4021) on feasibility of assumptions and measurement plan
decisions: Use RICE as the base (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) but multiply final RICE score by OpportunityFactor/(1+CostDeltaFactor) where OpportunityFactor = 1 + LatencyPenaltyScore and CostDeltaFactor = normalized expected marginal $/month per 1k tokens
LatencyPenaltyScore computed from customer cohorts: 0 (no penalty), 0.25 (minor), 0.5 (moderate), 1.0 (severe). Mapping guidance included in the playbook.
Confidence must include two components: data confidence (measurable telemetry) and engineering uncertainty (implementation risk). Use min(data_conf, eng_conf) in the formula to be conservative.
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs fidelity: we balance the need for a straightforward rubric usable in a 30-minute triage with the desire to accurately model token economics. We normalize cost to a per-1k-token delta to keep numbers comparable.
Latency impact is customer-perceived and sometimes non-linear; the ordinal penalty buckets capture tail sensitivity without requiring complex user-level modeling.
This model assumes a stable price per-token for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private work we include a flag and a default lower CostDeltaFactor since infra cost is amortized differently.
notes: Related artifacts: benchmarking spreadsheet in Drive (link below) with sample token cost curves pulled from runtime-1.18 tests.
We will pilot the rubric in the March roadmap cadence and iterate based on PM/Eng feedback.
This is intentionally conservative: initiatives with high latency penalties but small reach may surface higher urgency than pure RICE would show.
